name: Blues Point Tower
features: Lone 24-storey tower of 144 flats, meant as the forerunner of high-density housing on McMahons Point.
note: Wikipedia: construction finished late 1961 and first residents moved in 1962; 1962 used. Long called one of Sydney's ugliest buildings, which makes it a good discussion piece.

name: Grosvenor Place
features: 44-storey tower with column-free 2,000 m² floors; a diagonal walk passes two kept heritage buildings.
note: Photos are steep upward views; the first shows the curved tower and its splayed base columns best.

name: Bolte Bridge
features: Freeway bridge marked by two 140 m hollow concrete towers that stand free of the deck, purely as a gateway sign.

photos.file: File:Bolte Bridge Melbourne at twilight over Yarra River.jpg

note: A bridge rather than a building; included because the towers are a well-known DCM urban gesture. Drop if the wall should stay buildings only.

name: AAMI Park (Melbourne Rectangular Stadium)
features: 'Bioframe' roof of geodesic domes over the stands, letting light through to the pitch.
award: Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2011 national award

photos.file: File:AUS Melbourne, Central Business District, Olympic Park 004.jpg

note: The category also has a good interior view under the roof: File:AAMI Park Western Stand 99.jpg (CC BY-SA 3.0).

name: QV1
features: 40-storey tower with sunshades over its windows; free curving plaza buildings offset its strict geometry.

photos.file: File:AUS Perth, Central Business District, Milligan Street 002.jpg

note: Wikipedia notes awards for its energy efficiency. The category's 'Hay Street' photos show the curved plaza canopies (e.g. File:AUS Perth, Central Business District, Hay Street 005.jpg, CC BY 4.0) if a ground-level view is wanted.

name: Featherston House
features: One glass-walled room over an indoor garden, with platforms floating off the central chimney like a treehouse.
note: Only one usable exterior photo (house half-hidden in bush, which is the point of it). Two wide panoramas also exist but the house is tiny in them. The two drawings are student-made (2012) and generically named; check them before use.

name: Riverside Centre
features: 40-storey office tower above an open riverfront plaza with steps, cafés and a ferry wharf.

photos.file: File:Riparian Plaza 111 Eagle St and Riverside Centre from Petrie Bight Brisbane River P1260416.jpg
File:Riparian Plaza 111 Eagle St and Riverside Centre from Petrie Bight Brisbane River P1260417.jpg

note: Riverside Centre is the broad right-hand tower in both photos; Seidler's later Riparian Plaza (left, 2005) and 111 Eagle Street stand beside it. Most other category photos are skyline or Christmas-tree views, so no photo shows it alone.

name: Domain Park Flats
features: 20-storey slab facing the Botanic Gardens; windows and balconies are laid out freely to show each flat's size.
note: Photos are just above the 1200px minimum (about 1220x1650); the first shows the two lift towers. When finished it was the tallest residential building in Victoria.

name: Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law
features: Supreme and District Court tower that, with the Magistrates Court, fills a city block as a legal precinct.
award: Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2013 national award
commons_category: Category:Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law, Brisbane

photos.file: File:Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law, Brisbane, 2024, L3.jpg
File:Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law, Brisbane, 2024.jpg
File:Queen Elizabeth II Courts of Law seen from Albert Street, Brisbane 02.jpg

note: Wikipedia gives little on the design itself; the Key features line sticks to what it says.

name: National Portrait Gallery
features: Competition-winning gallery of simple day-lit rooms for about 500 portraits, entered under a deep coloured canopy.

photos.file: File:National Portrait Gallery, Canberra, Australia - Joy of Museums - Ext.jpg
File:National Portrait Gallery, Canberra, Australia - Joy of Museums - Ext 2.jpg

note: Only two exterior photos on Commons, both from one visit; the second is the entry court under the orange soffit.

name: RMIT Design Hub
by: Sean Godsell Architects with Peddle Thorp
features: Skin of sandblasted glass discs that a computer turns to control sun and heat, like a second wall.
award: Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2013 national award
note: Close-ups of the disc facade also exist: File:RMIT Design Hub detail.jpg (CC BY 2.0).

name: Swanston Academic Building (RMIT Building 80)
features: 11-storey teaching block wrapped in angled coloured panels meant to wear the 'cloak' of the city around it.
award: Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2013 national award

photos.file: File:SAB, Melbourne CBD, as viewed from Swanston Street.jpg

note: Wikipedia's infobox calls it Postmodern; Contemporary used here.

name: Melbourne School of Design (Glyn Davis Building)
features: Architecture school built as a teaching tool: exposed structure and a studio hall under a coffered timber roof.

photos.file: File:Melbourne University Faculty of Architecture, Building and Planning.jpg

note: No Wikipedia article; facts from project databases and ArchitectureAU (competition 2009, opened December 2014). Now called the Glyn Davis Building.

name: Ian Potter Museum of Art
features: University art museum whose grey street wall carries a frieze of broken classical fragments.

photos.file: File:Ian Potter Museum of Art exterior.JPG

note: Won the 1999 Victorian Architecture Medal (Wikipedia, citation needed). The frieze is an artwork on the facade; its artist is not named in the sources used.

name: South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute (SAHMRI)
features: Rounded research building nicknamed the 'cheese grater' for its skin of triangular facets, lifted on a glass base.
award: Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2014 national commendation
commons_category: Category:South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute

photos.file: File:South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute in Adelaide (028A1254).jpg
File:South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute in Adelaide (028A1263).jpg

note: Opened 29 November 2013.

name: Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies
features: Waterfront research 'shed' on Princes Wharf, its long folded roof lifting into a glazed end towards the harbour.
award: Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2014 national award
commons_category: Category:Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies

photos.file: File:Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies 20171117-003.jpg
File:Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies.jpg
File:Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies Hobart.jpg

note: Wikipedia's article is about the institute, not the building; year (opened early 2014) and architects from ArchitectureAU, Terroir and Engineers Australia.

name: Queensland Children's Hospital (former Lady Cilento Children's Hospital)
features: Hospital planned as a 'living tree' of trunks and branches, with green fins, roof gardens and terraces for daylight.
award: Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2015 national commendation

photos.file: File:Queensland Children's Hospital in Brisbane, November 2019.jpg
File:Lady Cilento Children’s Hospital, Brisbane, in June 2018, 03.jpg

note: Opened 29 November 2014 as Lady Cilento Children's Hospital; renamed 2018. A Conrad Gargett and Lyons joint venture.

name: Wellington Central Library (Te Matapihi)
features: Library on Civic Square with a curving glass wall behind a colonnade of metal nīkau-palm columns.
note: Closed 2019 over earthquake risk, strengthened and redesigned, reopened March 2026; the Civic Square front in the third photo is the new 2026 work, while the first two show Athfield's curved glass wall and nīkau columns. The nīkau columns are confirmed by the Commons category 'Nikau palm sculptures, Wellington' under Buildings by Athfield Architects. Avoid the 'Knjižnica' files: they show the old library next door (now City Gallery).

name: Palmerston North City Library
features: Old department store on The Square restored and extended as the city library, with angled steel and glass additions.

photos.file: File:Palmerston North City Library, Palmerston North, New Zealand 06.JPG

note: Wikipedia: the library is in 'the restored and extended C M Ross building', designed by Athfield and opened 1996 (his works list says 1997 for the extensions). The facade lettering reads 'The D.I.C. Ltd', so the building's names differ by source. The point for students is the adaptive reuse.

name: Art Gallery of New South Wales, North Building (Sydney Modern, Naala Nura)
features: Glass pavilions under thin roofs step down to Woolloomooloo Bay; a disused oil tank below became 'The Tank' gallery.
award: Sulman Medal 2023; Sir Zelman Cowen Award 2023 national award
note: Competition won by SANAA in 2015; opened December 2022. Two photos include a Yayoi Kusama flower sculpture on the terrace.

name: Geelong Library and Heritage Centre
features: Dome clad in 332 glass-reinforced concrete panels, nodding to the domed reading rooms of the great libraries.

photos.file: File:Dark Orb Geelong Library and Heritage Centre (48064055543).jpg

note: Opened 21 November 2015. The Wikipedia article does not name the architect; ARM Architecture is named in the Zelman Cowen Award list (2016 winner).

name: Melbourne Recital Centre
features: Concert hall with a cell-like glass and panel facade, holding a 1,000-seat 'modified shoebox' hall.

photos.file: File:Melbourne Recital Centre seen from the northeast.jpg

note: Built as one complex with the Melbourne Theatre Company's Southbank Theatre; acoustics by Arup. ARM's practice won the 2009 Victorian Architecture Medal (per the ARM article) but that article does not say for which project, so no award is claimed here.

name: Dorset Street Flats
features: Eight small flats with courtyards in load-bearing concrete block; a founding work of the Christchurch School.
note: Designed 1956, built 1956-57 (Warren's works list). Badly damaged in the 2011 earthquake and restored by Young Architects (2023 NZ Architecture Award); photos are from 2011-2016, before the restoration.

name: National Museum of Australia
by: Ashton Raggatt McDougall with Robert Peck von Hartel Trethowan
features: Building on a lake peninsula themed on knotted ropes; a giant loop at the entrance unrolls as the 'Uluru Axis'.

photos.file: File:National Museum of Australia aerial view.jpg

note: Opened 11 March 2001. Wikipedia names Howard Raggatt (ARM) as design architect, with Robert Peck von Hartel Trethowan, and describes the knotted-rope theme and the loop aligned with Uluru. Exterior photos are few and small (1500-1600px); most of the category shows museum objects.

name: Melbourne Museum
features: Two long sloping roof blades rise over the entrance, on axis with the 1880 Royal Exhibition Building opposite.
note: Opened 2000, construction completed 2001 per Wikipedia; 2000 used. Holds an indoor Forest Gallery. The building is hard to catch whole in one frame; photos show the entrance blades and the north face.

name: Michael Fowler Centre
by: Warren and Mahoney (Miles Warren, Maurice Mahoney)
features: Concert hall of tilted concrete panels over a glass circulation band, nicknamed the 'Squashed Top Hat'.
note: Opened September 1983; NZIA Enduring Architecture award 2010. Marked earthquake-prone in 2023, with demolition among the options proposed in 2024: its future is uncertain. The two 2018 photos are night views with coloured lighting on the panels.

name: Olympic Park Station
features: Station for Olympic crowds under a long vault of steel arches, open at the ends and lit from above.
award: Sulman Medal 1998; Sir Zelman Cowen Award 1998
note: Also won the 1998 BHP Colorbond steel award and the 2023 NSW Enduring Architecture Award.

name: Dixon Street Flats
features: Ten-storey state housing block of 115 flats with long access balconies; the archetype NZ modernist apartment block.
note: Ernst Plischke is popularly thought to have shaped the design, but Wikipedia says there is no documentary evidence, so only Wilson is credited. A historic CC BY 2.0 photo of the rooftop drying area also exists (File:State Housing, New Zealand (9721745436).jpg). 'Long access balconies' is read from the photos rather than the article.

name: Melbourne Exhibition Centre ('Jeff's Shed')
features: Long shed marked by a tilted metal entrance blade on yellow sticks and a 450 m verandah along the river.

photos.file: File:Melbourne Exhibition Centre viewed from the Yarra River.jpg

note: Opened 14 February 1996. Part of the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre; the 2009 Convention Centre next door is by Woods Bagot and NH Architecture, so avoid photos of that building.

name: Sky Tower
features: 328 m concrete telecom and observation tower on splayed legs, with a revolving restaurant at 190 m.
note: Built 1994-1997 as part of the SkyCity casino complex. 'Splayed legs' is read from the photos.

name: Aotea Centre
features: Performing arts centre on Aotea Square, its 2,139-seat theatre raised behind broad public stairs and a long veranda.

photos.file: File:Aotea Centre Off Aotea Square, Auckland.jpg

note: Designed 1974, built in the 1980s; main construction finished 1989 and opened 1990 (1990 used). The two public-domain photos are just 1600-1800px wide; the 2011 night photo shows the veranda added in the 2011 square upgrade.

name: Governor Phillip Tower
features: Granite and glass tower raised on zinc-plated beams over a sandstone podium, crowned by a steel 'milk-crate'.

photos.file: File:Quay Quarter Tower, Governor Phillip Tower, Sydney, 2023, 01.jpg
File:Quay Quarter Tower, Governor Phillip Tower, Sydney, 2023, 03.jpg

note: Completed 1993 (infobox; the complex is dated 1994 in the article text). In both photos it is the pale tower with the bladed top to the right of the newer, twisted Quay Quarter Tower; no Commons photo shows it alone. Built over the remains of the first Government House, now the Museum of Sydney.

name: Tūranga (Christchurch Central Library)
features: Post-earthquake central library on Cathedral Square, its glass box wrapped in tall folded fins.

photos.file: File:Exterior of Tūranga Central Library in Christchurch, New Zealand.jpg

note: Opened 12 October 2018 as one of the 17 anchor projects of the Christchurch rebuild. Not from a national award list. 'Folded fins' is read from the photos.
